title: Which decimal is the biggest?
hook: One has one digit after the point, one has two, one has three. Which counts for most?

doesNotKnow: how to compare decimals of different lengths

misconception: The decimal with more digits is bigger, so 0.125 > 0.25 > 0.3 ("longer is larger").
objective: The learner can explain that 0.3 > 0.25 > 0.125 because each decimal place is worth a tenth of the one before, so decimals are compared from the first digit after the point.

claims.text: 0.3 is 3 tenths, 0.25 is 2 tenths and 5 hundredths, and 0.125 is 1 tenth, 2 hundredths and 5 thousandths (stage: blocks, slivers and hairlines).
claims.source: Decimal notation: 0.3 = 3/10, 0.25 = 25/100, 0.125 = 125/1000. The stage adds digit d at place p as d pieces of width 10^-(p+1) on a 0-to-1 scale (true to scale).

claims.text: 0.3 is the largest of the three and its bar is the longest: 0.3 > 0.25 > 0.125 (300 > 250 > 125 thousandths).
claims.source: Convert to thousandths. node: [0.3, 0.25, 0.125].sort((a,b)=>a-b) = [0.125, 0.25, 0.3]. The stage computes values in integer thousandths (thousandths()) and the reveal names the largest from that sort.

claims.text: The five hundredth-slivers of 0.25 add 0.05, which is less than the one more tenth-block (0.1) it would need to reach 0.3.
Each decimal place is worth one tenth of the place to its left, so extra digits only add smaller and smaller pieces; compare decimals from the first digit after the point.
claims.source: Place value definition: the k-th place after the point is worth 10^-k. Because any digits after place k add less than one unit of place k (at most 0.0999… of it), the first differing digit decides.

claims.text: Stage legend: a block is 0.1, a sliver is 0.01 and a hairline is 0.001.
claims.source: Definition of the stage pieces (widths SCALE/10, SCALE/100, SCALE/1000 in Demo.tsx).

recall.question: Which is larger: 0.4 or 0.375?
recall.why: Compare from the first digit after the point: 4 tenths beat 3 tenths. The 75 thousandths of 0.375 add less than one more tenth.
